#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Making certain height based triangle
read -p "Enter height of the triangle :" height

echo "Presenting triagle specific for $height "

a=0
b=1
for ((i=1; i<=$height; i++));do
	# setting up the sequnce 1,1
	for ((j=1; j<=$i; j++));do
		# This prints the row of the triangle
		c=$(( a + b ))
		printf "%d " $c
		a=$b
		b=$c
		
	done
	echo ""
		
		
done

posts.name: Madhav Rimal
posts.cooked:
An seed for my own custom browser is been initiated so i had made a basic sed and tr pipeline which can turn a raw html into tokenizable format , i would make whole html tokenizer after exams

#!/usr/bin/env bash

read -p "Give your html file :" html_file
# Sanitization pipeline
cat $html_file |
  sed -n 's/ \+/ /p; /<script>/,/<\/script>/d; /<style/,/<\/style>/d' > sanitized

cat sanitized | grep -v '<!--.*' > sanitized_file
rm -frd sanitized 

# Making traversed html
cat sanitized_file | sed -n 's/ \+//p' | tr -s '>\(.*\)' '>/n\1' > traversed
cat traversed | tr -s '/n' > traversed_file # feding into tokenization program

Output : traversed_file which is ready for tokenization task ,

#Makingfromscratch

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Great work putting in the effort of using these tools by yourself for a bigger task. This is the one and only way to actually learn!

A few comments:

  • You do not need to do cat file | grep or cat file | sed or cat file | tr, all these commands can work on a file path given as command line argument.
  • You do not need to store each step as separate file (unless you want the intermediate outputs as well)
#!/usr/bin/env bash

read -p "Give your html file: " html_file

sed '
  s/ \+/ /g
  /<script>/,/<\/script>/d
  /<style>/,/<\/style>/d
' "$html_file" \
| grep -v '<!--.*' \
| sed 's/ \+//g' \
| sed 's/>/>\n/g' \
| tr -s '\n' \
> traversed_file

Further, not to discourage, but Regex can never fully parse XML.

Regex cannot parse XML because XML is defined by a context-free grammar (CFG) with recursive nesting, but regular expressions describe only regular languages (RG), which cannot express recursion.
Since XML requires matching arbitrarily nested tags, it exceeds the power of regular languages and needs a context-free parser.

Read the first answer to this, kind of an internet lore/meme.

posts.name: Madhav Rimal
posts.cooked:
Sure sir, I’ll keep these points in mind. I’m experimenting with building a very simple web browser that can handle basic HTML and present it using my own minimal rendering rules. The plan is to use curl for requests and redirects, then pass everything through a small sanitization + parsing pipeline so the final output stays clean and distraction-free.

Along with this, I’m working on a small wiki-corpus search engine by indexing responses from the public Wikipedia API and building a minimal retrieval layer on top of it. I plan to integrate this search engine directly into the browser so it has its own lightweight knowledge-retrieval system instead of depending on external search engines.

There are many ideas I want to explore, especially nested-structure handling and context-based grouping in HTML/XML for my mini engine. I’ll try my best to turn these experiments into something real.

Solving problem of distraction containing big browsers , my browser wont present big websites not a bug that would be a feature
